title: Directed Euler paths: in-degree equals out-degree characterization for directed graphs

problemStatement.formal: A connected digraph has an Eulerian circuit iff ∀ v, indeg(v) = outdeg(v). An Eulerian path from u to v exists iff outdeg(u) = indeg(u)+1, indeg(v) = outdeg(v)+1, and all other vertices balanced.
problemStatement.plain: Directed Euler path characterization: a directed graph has an Eulerian circuit iff every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree, and an Eulerian path iff exactly one source and one sink vertex have degree imbalance.
whyMatters: Natural generalization of Euler theorem to directed graphs
Foundation for de Bruijn sequences and DNA assembly algorithms
Connects directed and undirected Euler criteria
